nesnd_hus_registration.1.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_khanate').GetName] has been established. Indigenous settlers from Dongzhou and the United States have brought their families, possessions and hopes of keeping their land to the new country. The khan chosen by their communities depends on their support, and must defend the homes they have found.\n\nThe United States refuses to give up the land it ceded, and Dongzhou wants the plains back too. For the settlers, whether the khanate survives decides whether they must pack up and move yet again.
nesnd_american_restoration_reason: The restoration of the house of Moctezuma and the Andean court has won support among Indigenous villages. The republics promised liberty, yet their new rulers still encroach on common land and exact taxes. For those who work the fields, a change of flag in the capital has done little to lighten their burden.\n\nSupporters of the old dynasties are turning this resentment to their advantage. They promise to protect common land and local rights in return for the villages' people and arms. Rural communities, in turn, hope to use a monarch's prestige to resist the depredations of the new elite.
nesnd_native_restoration_war_reason: The restorationists have formed a separate government, bringing village militias together under the old dynasty's name to claim rule over the whole country. The former government refuses to surrender the territory that has broken away. War will now decide who protects the common lands, who collects the taxes and whose orders the army obeys.\n\nBoth sides mean to annex the other and refuse any peace that leaves the country divided.
nesnd_american_restoration.3.d: The army has broken up the restorationist meetings and cut the lines between local leaders. Those who wanted force are cheering; the Indigenous people hunted down in the searches are more certain than ever that this government protects only the men who took their land.\n\nThe movement has been beaten down for now, but the countryside's resentment runs deeper. The dynasty's supporters who escaped the soldiers will hardly let such an opportunity slip.
nesnd_american_restoration.3.a: Anyone else who gathers a crowd will get the same.
nesnd_american_restoration.5.d: The opposing government has lost its last territory, and the country is reunited. The army is taking control of the provinces. Taxes collected by rival authorities during the war will once again be sent to a single capital.\n\nMany in the countryside followed the losing side. Its flag has come down, but their convictions have not come down with it.
nesnd_american_restoration.6.d: Changes in territory and government have cut the restoration struggle short. Our rival can no longer fight on, yet we have not taken all of its lands.\n\nWe must work out anew who is friend and who is foe, and settle the unfinished local questions within the new borders.
nesnd_american_restoration.10.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_restoration_applicant').GetName] proposes that both countries recognise the existing Inca court and that its territory be joined to ours. A shared dynastic tradition has given their representatives and ours a basis on which to discuss union.\n\nTheir local communities would come under our rule along with the land, counting on the court to protect their common land and local rights.
nesnd_khanate_emergence_reason: The American Civil War has shaken authority on the Great Plains, while Dongzhou's new registration law has brought Indigenous grievances to the fore. Community leaders are renewing ties with supporters of the earlier uprising, hoping to use the upheaval in both countries to establish a khanate of their own.\n\nThis alliance is rooted in land. Where people move and how they are registered decide where they can survive. To win the communities' loyalty, a new khan must first promise to defend these things, and then have the strength to keep both powers out.
nesnd_khanate_survival_reason: The United States and Dongzhou both demand the khanate's annexation. Indigenous people who have only just settled on the Plains must take up arms again to defend the homes they struggled to obtain. Having acclaimed a common khan, the communities expect him to unite their scattered forces against the two invaders.\n\nThe new khan needs their men and their grain; the local leaders want to keep their own rights. War has knotted the peoples together, and if the knot comes loose, they will have to leave these plains.
nesnd_suppress_native_khanate_reason: Since the Great Plains were ceded, migrating peoples have poured onto the grasslands. With the backing of Indigenous communities, the khanate has set up a government and means to twist settlers, land and local militias into a single state. Let it put down roots, and our claim to this land will grow weaker by the year.\n\nWe will annex the khanate. The new khan, for his part, hopes to drive off the interveners and use a victory to stamp the Plains Compact's authority on every band.
nesnd_native_khanate.2.d: Both interventions are over, and the khanate has kept its government. The communities stood together against outside powers, and the settlers have finally made a home on the Plains.\n\nNow the new khan must talk taxes, defence and power with the local leaders. The quarrels shelved in wartime are being laid back on the table, one by one.
nesnd_native_khanate.3.d: From the northern plains to the southern mountains, the Americas now answer to one government. The former state of Dongzhou is gone. The new [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] has inherited its name, abolished the old social hierarchy and assumed rule over the continent as a republic.\n\nIndigenous peoples who once ran from office to office for land, status and local rights are now the masters of this country. A republic this large is theirs to carry from now on.
nesnd_a2_exodus_both_desc: With registration complete, Manchu and Mongol communities left in the second tier have begun to leave the republic. Some have gone to [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_cne_country').GetName], others to the west of [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_a2_usa_country').GetName], carrying their families and old ties to new lands.\n\nEach community has a seventy percent chance of choosing the former destination and thirty percent of choosing the latter. In the end, the equal registration they waited for never came.
nesnd_american_restoration.11.d: The deadline has passed, and the Inca court never agreed to union. For all their shared dynastic tradition, the two governments still each rule their own land and people.\n\nTalks can be reopened later. For now, the two states stand apart as before.
nesnd_american_restoration.12.d: The Inca court has turned down the union. The two houses share a dynastic tradition and can call each other kin, but neither will give up its throne or its court.\n\nVillage land and local quarrels are still ours to deal with; we cannot wait on an answer from the court. Once the waiting period has ended, we may send envoys again.
nesnd_american_restoration.13.d: The dynasty's supporters have called the local communities together again to settle the terms between court and countryside. The restoration's legitimacy is established, but local leaders still want to know exactly where their land and their representatives stand under the new rule.\n\nThe court needs the villages behind it, and the villages need the court to protect them. This compact must be honoured in every tax and every levy of troops.
nesnd_native_khanate.2.both: Both intervening governments have been forced to accept humiliation, and the khanate has preserved its government. The victory of the Army of the Plains Compact has brought prestige to the union between the new khan and the communities. Settlers can remain in their new homes.\n\nNow that the fighting is over, they must agree on how to raise taxes, how to share the burden of defence and which rights stay with each community. Battles already won will not hold up a lasting government.
nesnd_native_khanate.2.one: One intervention ended in the opponent's humiliation, and the other has also come to a close. The khanate has preserved its government and territory. Those who settled here can remain and earn their living on the Plains.\n\nThe communities gathered under the new khan's banner to hold off invasion; now the talk is of taxes, defence and local power. In war, everyone shouldered the load together; in peace, each will want to see what share comes to him.
nesnd_native_khanate.2.none: Both interventions have ended. The khanate forced neither opponent to accept humiliation, but it has preserved its government. The communities of the Plains can continue to build their new homes.\n\nThe new khan still leans on the local leaders and the settlers. How taxes and defence are shared out, and how each district's rights are kept: on these few things hangs a compact made to survive.
nesnd_native_khanate.4.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_khanate_opponent').GetName] has withdrawn from treaties with the khanate containing an alliance or defensive pact, clearing the way for intervention. Promises once intended to secure both countries have given way to demands for annexation and territory.\n\nAny trade or other provisions within those treaties end with them, and the withdrawing country bears the cost of breaking its word.
nesnd_american_restoration.14.d: Supporters of the old dynasty have established ties with Indigenous villages. Local leaders are gathering recruits and supplies, hoping a new government will protect their lands and autonomy. The restorationists intend to use this rural strength to restore the dynasty's rule.\n\nThe preparations will take twelve months. The government of [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] can still win over the villages with talks on local councils and land rights; the longer it waits, the better organised the restorationists become.
nesnd_journal_closures_parent_cne: This matter is closed together with “$ce_cne_land_reform$”.
nesnd_journal_closures_parent_qin: This debate at court closes together with “$nesnd_qe1_agenda_journal$”.
nesnd_journal_closures_restoration_concl: The talks on Indigenous restoration end here.
nesnd_journal_closures_america_conclusio: The continental plan to expand at $HUS$'s expense has run its course.
nesnd_journal_closures_india_society_con: The effort to build a common Indian identity has been left unfinished.
nesnd_journal_closures_india_princes_con: This Indian princely state's foreign dealings end here.
nesnd_journal_closures_india_usm_conclus: Our direct rule over Tianzhu ends here.
nesnd_journal_closures_india_dynasty_con: The effort to hold loyalty through the dynasty's prestige has come to an end.
nesnd_journal_closures_india_france_conc: Our dealings with France and the French advisers' commission are both over.
nesnd_journal_closures_india_uprising_co: Our contacts with the uprising networks are cut off here.
nesnd_journal_closures_japan_cohesion_co: The former Japanese state is gone, and the national cohesion it led has lapsed with it.
nesnd_journal_closures_japan_foreign_con: The former Japanese state's envoys are no longer abroad.
nesnd_journal_closures_ottoman_recovery_: The military and political order that the recovery policy held up has fallen apart.
nesnd_journal_closures_ottoman_unity_con: The Ottoman state's former cohesion policy ends here.
nesnd_journal_closures_persia_west_concl: The plan to push west with Western Qin's help has been abandoned.
nesnd_journal_closures_persia_east_concl: The plan to challenge Western Qin's eastern frontier has been dropped.
nesnd_journal_closures_persia_governance: The former Persian government's special grants have stopped.
nesnd_journal_closures_qin_court_conclus: The court debate among the imperial house, the literati and the army has broken up.
nesnd_journal_closures_qin_unity_conclus: The old means of holding Western Qin's lands to a common identity end here.
nesnd_india_society_reason: Living in one country does not make people compatriots. The provinces have their own languages, faiths and princes of old. Now that schools and cities are growing, people have begun to argue: who has the right to speak for India? The dynasty, the local leaders and the rising national movement each have their own answer.
nesnd_india_princes_reason: Delhi, Nanjing and Paris have each named their terms to the Indian princes. The princes mean to keep more than their ancestral palaces: their land, their revenue and the fate of their own states. No one's help comes free.
nesnd_india_foreign_reason: France wants to keep its hold on India through trade, investment and military aid; Delhi is short of teachers, engineers and officers. The specialists trained under French instruction will be our own, but our patron will still be Paris.
nesnd_india_foreign_status: Take France's help, but keep our own counsel.
nesnd_india_diplomacy.2.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('india_partner').GetName] has accepted our request. The agreement has been put into effect.
nesnd_india_diplomacy.3.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('india_partner').GetName] has turned down the delegation's terms. We will have to find another way.
nesnd_india_diplomacy.1.d1: [SCOPE.sCountry('india_sender').GetName] asks France to send teachers and to fund its first few schools. They want specialists of their own; and once French advisers are in the classrooms, France's weight in their education grows too.
nesnd_india_diplomacy.1.d2: [SCOPE.sCountry('india_sender').GetName] asks France to send mining and industrial engineers and to fund new industries. They want the new methods of production; French firms have their eye on the business.
nesnd_india_diplomacy.1.d3: [SCOPE.sCountry('india_sender').GetName] asks France to send military instructors and help pay to reorganise its army. They want an army worth the name; France would get the chance to set that army's rules for years to come.
nesnd_india_diplomacy.1.d4: The envoys of [SCOPE.sCountry('india_sender').GetName] ask for greater autonomy, so that their own government can handle more of its affairs.
nesnd_india_revolt.1.d: Opponents of colonial rule in [SCOPE.sState('india_case_state').GetName] have risen openly, seized the local offices and declared they no longer obey their old rulers. Whether to recognise the breakaway has become a dispute between two states.
nesnd_india_dynasty_journal_reason: The dynasty's old prestige still counts, but people also weigh their sovereign by the government in front of them. Whether the provinces' faiths are respected, and whether Delhi can make up its own mind, will decide whether the provinces still stand by this dynasty.
